**Sikhae (Seaweed Soup) – A Simple Korean Recipe** *This is a quick, comforting soup that’s perfect for a light meal or as an accompaniment to rice.* --- ### Ingredients | Item | Amount | |------|--------| | **Kelp (seaweed)** | 1 sheet (about 5 cm × 15 cm) | | **Water** | 2 cups (480 ml) | | **Soy sauce** | 1 tablespoon | | **Salt** | ½ teaspoon (adjust to taste) | | **Optional add‑ons** | • Thinly sliced scallions
• Toasted sesame seeds
• Sliced mushrooms or tofu (for extra protein)
• A pinch of pepper or chili flakes | --- ### Instructions 1. **Prepare the Kelp** - Rinse the kelp under cold water to remove any grit. - Cut it into bite‑sized strips or leave it whole if you prefer a more rustic texture. 2. **Boil the Water** - In a small pot, bring 2 cups of water to a gentle boil over medium heat. 3. **Add the Kelp** - Once the water is boiling, drop the kelp pieces in. - Reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for about 5 minutes. - If you’re adding mushrooms or tofu, toss them in now so they can soften with the kelp. 4. **Season** - Stir in 1 tablespoon of soy sauce and ½ teaspoon of salt. - Taste and adjust seasoning—add a little more soy sauce for saltiness or a pinch of pepper for heat. 5. **Finish & Serve** - Remove from heat. - Ladle the soup into bowls. - Garnish with thinly sliced scallions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds if desired. - Serve hot, ideally with steamed white rice or as part of a larger Korean spread. --- ### Tips & Variations - **Texture Preference:** If you like a smoother soup, blend the kelp after cooking. - **Flavor Boost:** Add a splash of mirin or a dash of fish sauce for depth. - **Protein Upgrade:** Add diced chicken breast or shrimp during step 3 for a heartier dish. - **Vegetarian Option:** Use vegetable broth instead of plain water and add tofu cubes for extra protein. Enjoy your homemade sikhae! It’s simple, nutritious, and captures the essence of Korean seaweed dishes.
